```{python}
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

print("[1/6] Importing PySpark...", flush=True)
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

os.environ["PYSPARK_PYTHON"] = sys.executable
os.environ["PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON"] = sys.executable

print("[2/6] Starting Spark session...", flush=True)
spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .appName("JobPostingsAnalysis")
    .master("local[*]")
    .config("spark.driver.host", "localhost")
    .getOrCreate()
)
print("[3/6] Spark session ready.", flush=True)

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled", "false")

# Use the full dataset for the final analysis.
USE_SAMPLE = False

candidate_dirs = [
    Path("../data/MET_CareerCompass_2026"),
    Path("data/MET_CareerCompass_2026"),
    Path(r"E:\Data\Jobs\_2026\_Refined"),
]
data_dir = next((path.resolve() for path in candidate_dirs if path.exists()), None)
if data_dir is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Dataset directory not found. Checked: "
        + ", ".join(str(path.resolve()) for path in candidate_dirs)
    )

print(f"[4/6] Looking for Parquet files in {data_dir}...", flush=True)
parquet_files = sorted(data_dir.glob("*.parquet"))
if not parquet_files:
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No Parquet files found in {data_dir}")

if USE_SAMPLE:
    parquet_files = parquet_files[:1]
print(f"[5/6] Reading {len(parquet_files)} Parquet file(s)...", flush=True)
df = spark.read.parquet(*[str(path) for path in parquet_files])

# Parquet columns are uppercase; normalize once so the rest of the notebook can use lowercase names.
df = df.toDF(*[column.lower() for column in df.columns])
df.createOrReplaceTempView("job_postings")

print("[6/6] Data loaded and registered as job_postings.", flush=True)
df.printSchema()
df.show(5)
```

```{python}
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, monotonically_increasing_id


companies = (
    df.select(
        col("company_name").alias("company"),
        "company_name",
        "company_raw",
        "company_is_staffing",
    )
    .distinct()
    .withColumn("company_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    .select(
        "company_id",
        "company",
        "company_name",
        "company_raw",
        "company_is_staffing",
    )
)

industries = (
    df.select(
        "naics_2022_6",
        "naics_2022_6_name",
        "soc_5",
        "soc_5_name",
        "onet_name",
        "soc_2_name",
    )
    .distinct()
    .withColumn("industry_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    .select(
        "industry_id",
        "naics_2022_6",
        "naics_2022_6_name",
        "soc_5",
        "soc_5_name",
        "onet_name",
        "soc_2_name",
    )
)

locations = (
    df.select(
        "location",
        "city_name",
        "state_name",
        "county_name",
        "msa",
        "msa_name",
    )
    .distinct()
    .withColumn("location_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    .select(
        "location_id",
        "location",
        "city_name",
        "state_name",
        "county_name",
        "msa",
        "msa_name",
    )
)

print(flush=True)
job_postings = (
    df.alias("j")
    .join(
        companies.alias("c"),
        col("j.company_name").eqNullSafe(col("c.company_name"))
        & col("j.company_raw").eqNullSafe(col("c.company_raw"))
        & col("j.company_is_staffing").eqNullSafe(col("c.company_is_staffing")),
        "left",
    )
    .join(
        industries.alias("i"),
        col("j.naics_2022_6").eqNullSafe(col("i.naics_2022_6"))
        & col("j.naics_2022_6_name").eqNullSafe(col("i.naics_2022_6_name"))
        & col("j.soc_5").eqNullSafe(col("i.soc_5"))
        & col("j.soc_5_name").eqNullSafe(col("i.soc_5_name"))
        & col("j.onet_name").eqNullSafe(col("i.onet_name"))
        & col("j.soc_2_name").eqNullSafe(col("i.soc_2_name")),
        "left",
    )
    .join(
        locations.alias("l"),
        col("j.location").eqNullSafe(col("l.location"))
        & col("j.city_name").eqNullSafe(col("l.city_name"))
        & col("j.state_name").eqNullSafe(col("l.state_name"))
        & col("j.county_name").eqNullSafe(col("l.county_name"))
        & col("j.msa").eqNullSafe(col("l.msa"))
        & col("j.msa_name").eqNullSafe(col("l.msa_name")),
        "left",
    )
    .select(
        col("j.id").alias("id"),
        col("j.title_clean"),
        col("c.company_id"),
        col("i.industry_id"),
        col("j.employment_type_name"),
        col("j.remote_type_name"),
        col("j.body"),
        col("j.min_years_experience"),
        col("j.max_years_experience"),
        col("j.salary"),
        col("j.salary_from"),
        col("j.salary_to"),
        col("l.location_id"),
        col("j.posted"),
        col("j.expired"),
        col("j.duration"),
    )
)

# Register all four relational tables for Spark SQL queries.
companies.createOrReplaceTempView("companies")
industries.createOrReplaceTempView("industries")
locations.createOrReplaceTempView("locations")
job_postings.createOrReplaceTempView("job_postings")
job_postings.createOrReplaceTempView("met_career_compass_records")

print(flush=True)
for table_name, table_df in {
    "job_postings": job_postings,
    "companies": companies,
    "industries": industries,
    "locations": locations,
}.items():
    print(f"- {table_name}: {table_df.count():,} rows", flush=True)

companies.show(5, truncate=False)
industries.show(5, truncate=False)
locations.show(5, truncate=False)
job_postings.show(5, truncate=False)
```

```{python}
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from pathlib import Path

salary_trends = spark.sql("""
    WITH salary_data AS (
        SELECT
            i.naics_2022_6_name AS industry_name,
            i.specialized_occupation,
            COALESCE(
                try_cast(regexp_replace(j.salary_from, '[^0-9.]', '') AS DOUBLE),
                try_cast(regexp_replace(j.salary_to, '[^0-9.]', '') AS DOUBLE)
            ) AS salary_value
        FROM job_postings AS j
        INNER JOIN industries AS i
            ON j.industry_id = i.industry_id
        WHERE i.naics_2022_6 = '518210'
    )
    SELECT
        industry_name,
        specialized_occupation,
        percentile_approx(salary_value, 0.5) AS median_salary,
        COUNT(*) AS posting_count
    FROM salary_data
    WHERE salary_value IS NOT NULL
      AND salary_value > 0
      AND specialized_occupation IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY industry_name, specialized_occupation
    ORDER BY median_salary DESC
    LIMIT 20
""")

print("Top 20 median salary trends:")
salary_trends.show(20, truncate=False)

salary_trends_pd = salary_trends.toPandas()
fig = px.bar(
    salary_trends_pd,
    x="median_salary",
    y="specialized_occupation",
    orientation="h",
    hover_data=["posting_count"],
    text="median_salary",
    title="Top 20 Median Salaries in Technology Industry",
    labels={
        "median_salary": "Median Salary",
        "specialized_occupation": "Specialized Occupation",
        "posting_count": "Job Postings",
    },
)
fig.update_traces(
    marker_color="#2f6f8f",
    texttemplate="$%{text:,.0f}",
    textposition="inside",
    insidetextanchor="middle",
    textfont={"size": 10, "color": "white"},
)
fig.update_layout(
    autosize=True,
    height=760,
    bargap=0.18,
    margin={"l": 285, "r": 35, "t": 65, "b": 55},
    font={"size": 11},
    xaxis={"tickprefix": "$", "tickformat": ",.0f", "automargin": True},
    yaxis={"categoryorder": "total ascending", "automargin": True},
)

output_dir = Path("output")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
chart_path = output_dir / "technology_median_salary_trends.html"
fig.write_html(chart_path, auto_open=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn")
print(f"Interactive Plotly chart saved to {chart_path}")
display(HTML(fig.to_html(include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=False, config={"responsive": True})))
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

remote_ca = spark.sql("""
    SELECT
        c.company_name,
        COUNT(*) AS remote_jobs
    FROM job_postings AS j
    INNER JOIN companies AS c
        ON j.company_id = c.company_id
    INNER JOIN locations AS l
        ON j.location_id = l.location_id
    WHERE j.remote_type_name = 'Remote'
      AND l.state_name = 'California'
    GROUP BY c.company_name
    ORDER BY remote_jobs DESC
""")

top_remote_ca = remote_ca.limit(5)
print("Top companies hiring for remote jobs in CA:")
top_remote_ca.show(truncate=False)

top_remote_ca_pd = top_remote_ca.toPandas()
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(
    data=top_remote_ca_pd,
    x="company_name",
    y="remote_jobs",
    hue="company_name",
    palette="deep",
    legend=False,
)
plt.title("Top Companies Hiring for Remote Jobs in CA")
plt.xlabel("Company Name")
plt.ylabel("Remote Jobs")
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.tight_layout()

output_dir = Path("output")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
remote_chart_path = output_dir / "top_remote_companies_ca.png"
plt.savefig(remote_chart_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print(f"Seaborn chart saved to {remote_chart_path}")
```

```{python}
from pyspark.sql.functions import to_date
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

monthly_ca = spark.sql("""
    WITH dated_records AS (
        SELECT
            to_date(j.posted, 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS posted_date
        FROM job_postings AS j
        INNER JOIN locations AS l
            ON j.location_id = l.location_id
        WHERE l.state_name = 'California'
    )
    SELECT
        year(posted_date) AS year,
        month(posted_date) AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS job_count
    FROM dated_records
    WHERE posted_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY year(posted_date), month(posted_date)
    ORDER BY year DESC, month DESC
""")

print("Monthly California record trends:")
monthly_ca.show(50, truncate=False)

monthly_ca_pd = monthly_ca.toPandas().sort_values(["year", "month"])
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(11, 6))
sns.lineplot(
    data=monthly_ca_pd,
    x="month",
    y="job_count",
    hue="year",
    marker="o",
    palette="deep",
)
plt.xticks(
    range(1, 13),
    ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"],
)
plt.title("Monthly Met Career Compass Records in CA")
plt.xlabel("Month")
plt.ylabel("Job Count")
plt.legend(title="Year")
plt.tight_layout()

output_dir = Path("output")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
monthly_chart_path = output_dir / "monthly_california_record_trends.png"
plt.savefig(monthly_chart_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print(f"Seaborn chart saved to {monthly_chart_path}")
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

metro_salary = spark.sql("""
    WITH metro_map(metro_area, search_term) AS (
        VALUES
            ('Boston', 'boston'),
            ('Washington DC', 'washington'),
            ('New York', 'new york'),
            ('San Francisco', 'san francisco'),
            ('Seattle', 'seattle'),
            ('Los Angeles', 'los angeles'),
            ('Dallas', 'dallas'),
            ('Houston', 'houston'),
            ('Austin', 'austin'),
            ('Nashville', 'nashville'),
            ('Kansas City', 'kansas city'),
            ('Denver', 'denver')
    ),
    metro_records AS (
        SELECT
            m.metro_area,
            COALESCE(
                try_cast(regexp_replace(j.salary_from, '[^0-9.]', '') AS DOUBLE),
                try_cast(regexp_replace(j.salary_to, '[^0-9.]', '') AS DOUBLE)
            ) AS salary_value
        FROM job_postings AS j
        INNER JOIN locations AS l
            ON j.location_id = l.location_id
        INNER JOIN metro_map AS m
            ON lower(concat_ws(
                ' ',
                coalesce(l.location, ''),
                coalesce(l.city_name, ''),
                coalesce(l.msa_name, '')
            )) LIKE concat('%', m.search_term, '%')
    ),
    metro_summary AS (
        SELECT
            metro_area,
            ROUND(AVG(salary_value), 2) AS average_salary,
            COUNT(*) AS record_count
        FROM metro_records
        WHERE salary_value IS NOT NULL
          AND salary_value > 0
        GROUP BY metro_area
    )
    SELECT
        m.metro_area,
        COALESCE(s.average_salary, 0) AS average_salary,
        COALESCE(s.record_count, 0) AS record_count
    FROM metro_map AS m
    LEFT JOIN metro_summary AS s
        ON m.metro_area = s.metro_area
    ORDER BY average_salary DESC
""")

print("Average salaries across selected major US metros:")
metro_salary.show(truncate=False)

metro_salary_pd = metro_salary.toPandas()
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
sns.barplot(
    data=metro_salary_pd,
    x="metro_area",
    y="average_salary",
    hue="metro_area",
    palette="deep",
    legend=False,
)
plt.title("Average Salary Across Selected Major US Metro Areas")
plt.xlabel("Metropolitan Area")
plt.ylabel("Average Salary")
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_formatter(
    plt.matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter("${x:,.0f}")
)
plt.tight_layout()

output_dir = Path("output")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
metro_chart_path = output_dir / "average_salary_major_metros.png"
plt.savefig(metro_chart_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print(f"Seaborn chart saved to {metro_chart_path}")
```
